Docs/Policy integration

Policy integration

Connect a policy to the released environment without changing its input, action or success contract.

Start from an existing evaluator

The six scored methods already have evaluation entry points. Prefer those paths when reproducing a released checkpoint: they restore model-specific image processing, temporal history, action execution and result recording. Evaluation provides the commands; train/TRAIN_EVAL.md ↗ describes ACT, Diffusion Policy, PPO and RLPD.

A new policy needs an explicit adapter. Define which observations it consumes, how its outputs become controller targets, when a chunk is refreshed, and which reset event clears its state. Merely matching the tensor width does not establish a compatible policy.

Discover the native interface

import gymnasium as gym
import tasks
from utils.dex_scene_eval import registered_task_settings

env_id = "OfficeDeskClickMouse-Sharpa-v1"
env = gym.make(env_id, **registered_task_settings(env_id),
               obs_mode="state", num_envs=1, sim_backend="physx_cpu")
try:
    observation, info = env.reset(seed=10001)
    print(env.observation_space)
    print(env.action_space)
finally:
    env.close()

This is an environment-interface check, not a learned-policy score. Image agents must construct their method's fixed camera rig before creating the environment. Read task state and channel names from the selected environment and dataset metadata; object-state fields must not leak into an image policy that was trained without them.

Keep model coordinates separate from joint targets

The released Sharpa demonstrations store absolute pd_joint_pos targets in radians: 29 values for one arm and hand, 58 for both. For the dual robot the controller order is left arm, right arm, left hand, right hand. Use utils/dex_tasks.py ↗ and the live controller binding to obtain the actual named layout.

RLPD's residual actions, GR00T's modality transforms and π0.5's asynchronous queue are model interfaces, not changes to the task's native controller. Preserve their conversions rather than sending normalized or relative outputs straight to env.step. π0.5 checks named joints, cameras and the controller through utils/pi05_utils/binding.py ↗.

Reset model state and retain every outcome

Clear action queues, recurrent state, temporal ensembles and instruction caches on every environment reset. Handle termination and time limits separately. Accumulate whether the task's info["success"] became true during the episode; also retain final-step success when diagnosing replay, since the two can differ.

Use the registered horizon for a full benchmark run and save one record per requested seed. A short wiring run, a random action sample or an infrastructure error is not a policy score. Review the protocol and checkpoint limitations before comparing your result with the leaderboard.
